issue_context.title: Add device condition support to the alarm_control_panel integration
issue_context.body:
Add [device condition](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/device_automation_condition.html) support to the alarm_control_panel integration.

Device conditions are part of [Device Automations](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/device_automation_index.html), a new concept that was [recently launched](https://www.home-assistant.io/blog/2019/09/18/release-99/#device-automations) to make automations more user friendly.

Device automations consist of three different parts: triggers, conditions and conditions. This issue is about the condition part.

To get started with this issue, you will need to set up a Home Assistant development environment. The easiest approach is to get started using [a dev container](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/development_environment.html#developing-with-devcontainer).

Once you have a development environment set up, run the following and follow the instructions:

```python
python3 -m script.scaffold device_condition
```

_(This issue is part of #26994)_

In principle I agree with you, but in this case I do not think that it is useful to change this because doing something like this
```python
base_dict.copy().update({CONF_TYPE: CONDITION_DISARMED})
```
for every condition does not make the code more readable IMHO.

It easier for me to read since I can quickly see what is different between the lines and don't have to process each block in my head to find the most important part.  That being said, I'm not the only one reading the code so its just my opinion and certainly not a requirement.
This should not be an `elif` statement.

It looks like `SUPPORT_ALARM_ARM_CUSTOM_BYPASS` isn't accounted for.  It doesn't appear to be used in anything but 
`homeassistant/components/manual/alarm_control_panel.py:    SUPPORT_ALARM_ARM_CUSTOM_BYPASS`
It looks like `state` will be undefined here if `config_validation` was true.
